title: CPOT (Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool)
sources: Gélinas C et al. Am J Crit Care 2006; SCCM PADIS 2018 guideline (recommended tool)
purpose: Observational pain assessment for critically ill adults unable to self-report. Four domains, 0–2 each (total 0–8). Use alongside RASS (arousal), not instead of it. A score > 2 indicates significant pain and should drive analgesia titration.

options.label: Tense — brow lowering, orbit tightening, levator contraction (1)
Grimacing — all of the above plus eyelids tightly closed (2)
Protection — slow cautious movements, touching/rubbing the pain site (1)
Restlessness — pulling at tubes, attempting to sit up, thrashing, not following commands (2)

items.label: Muscle tension (passive flexion/extension of the arm)

options.label: Tense, rigid — resistance to passive movement (1)
Very tense or rigid — strong resistance, unable to complete (2)

items.label: Compliance with the ventilator (intubated) OR vocalisation (extubated)

options.label: Tolerating ventilator / speaking in a normal tone or silent (0)
Fighting the ventilator, alarms frequently triggered / crying out, sobbing (2)

interpretation.label: Acceptable — minimal or no pain behaviours. Maintain current analgesia; reassess per protocol and before/after procedures

Significant pain — give an analgesic bolus and up-titrate the infusion; treat procedural pain pre-emptively. Reassess in 15–30 min. Rule out a new surgical / ischaemic / compartment cause if the score jumps

notes: Analgesia-first / analgosedation: treat pain before deepening sedation. Validated in medical, surgical, and trauma ICU patients; less reliable in brain injury and deep neuromuscular blockade (behaviours are abolished — use physiologic trend and assume pain during noxious care). Pair with a daily target, RASS, and a delirium screen (CAM-ICU / ICDSC).
